cases.name: memory: heapsnapshot analysis advanced
cases.about: The 5 advanced --memoryDebugging heap snapshot analysis tools on deterministic V8 fixtures (sample + sample_v2): retaining paths (full + depth limit + missing node), duplicate strings (normal + truncated), query objects (className regex, propertyName, nodeType, retainedSize/selfSize ranges, isDetached, sortBy), compare_heapsnapshots (summary + detailed classIndex + invalid classIndex), and analyze_heapsnapshot_contexts (live vs dead fields, scriptsWithoutScopes, retainedSize & scopeInfoNodeId filters).

visible: true asks whether the matched text is visible - a computed style and a non-empty bounding box (Puppeteer's checkVisibility) - and Crane has no layout (needs-renderer); Crane answers "visible is not supported by Crane's MCP server: Crane has no layout to tell whether text is visible."

The request headers differ as in "network: list, filter, details" call 5 (Chrome's UA client hints and user-agent; Blink's header order), Crane's POST carries no content-length request header (a Network domain finding, queued by main 2026-11-24), and the response's date header is the second it was served. The bodies' sections and the saved files are compared: the files listing must be equal.

Not a file input: chrome-devtools-mcp clicks the element and waits 3 s for a file chooser (Page.setInterceptFileChooserDialog); element clicks are batch 5, so Crane says no click happened (main's ruling 3, 2026-11-24). Batch 5 switches to Google's text and the file-chooser path.

expected.case: history: back right after the first navigation
expected.reason: Chrome navigates its startup URL (Puppeteer starts it with about:blank: an auto_toplevel entry), so its first navigation pushes and back reaches about:blank; Firefox 159 and Safari 27.2 keep the first tab's initial about:blank, which the first navigation replaces (WebDriver probe, chat.local 2026-11-24, tmp/probes/mcp1-startup/run.sh: history.length stays 1, back() stays), as Crane and HTML do: the browser majority (main's ruling, 2026-11-24).
Geolocation needs Crane's Geolocation API (a 0.1 spec item main queued, 2026-11-24); until then Crane's MCP server says it does not support geolocation yet.
